can.title: Pineapple Express
can.reason: A running thread of the film's jokes — including a fake sequel pitch — assumes you've seen it.

can.title: Superbad
can.reason: The cast play exaggerated versions of the personas they built here.

must.title: Captain America: Civil War
must.reason: Civil War fractures the Avengers and scatters them as fugitives — Infinity War assumes you know why Cap, Widow and Falcon are on the run and why Tony won't speak to them.

must.title: Thor: Ragnarok
must.reason: Asgard is destroyed and its survivors are refugees in space when Infinity War opens — that's where Ragnarok left them, along with Loki holding the Tesseract and Hulk refusing to resurface as Banner.

must.title: Ant-Man and the Wasp
must.reason: The Quantum Realm mechanics that make Endgame's time-travel plan possible — and how Scott Lang ends up trapped there during the five-year gap — are set up here.

from.title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

must.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
must.reason: The multiverse-fracturing spell Doctor Strange casts — and the price he's already paid for meddling with reality — is the direct fallout of No Way Home.

must.title: WandaVision
must.reason: Wanda's command of chaos magic, her discovery of the Darkhold, and her broken state after losing her sons and Vision all carry over directly from this show.

can.title: Dawn of the Dead
can.reason: A deliberate homage to Romero's zombie-siege structure — the pub standoff mirrors the mall siege beat for beat, right down to specific shots.

can.title: The Shining
can.reason: An entire extended sequence recreates the Overlook Hotel in exacting detail — the twins, the elevator, the hedge maze — and lands harder if you recognise it shot for shot.

can.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
can.reason: The opening sequence is a direct parody of 2001's 'Dawn of Man' — same framing, same music cue, same beat where a tool gets flung into the air.

can.title: Point Break
can.reason: The characters watch and explicitly discuss this film on-screen, and the plot's late turn deliberately mirrors its beats.

can.title: Bad Boys II
can.reason: Referenced by name in dialogue as the model for the film's own over-the-top action-movie climax.

must.title: Thunderbolts*
must.reason: Doomsday's 'New Avengers' team — Bucky, Yelena, Walker, Ghost, Red Guardian and Sentry/Void — is the team assembled at the end of this film; you need to know who they are and how they got the name.

must.title: The Fantastic 4: First Steps
must.reason: This film ends with Reed Richards' family crossing out of their own universe into the mainline MCU — that's why the Fantastic Four are suddenly present in Doomsday's story at all.

must.title: The Mandalorian
must.reason: Direct continuation of Din Djarin and Grogu's story, picking up their bond and the New Republic setting established across three seasons.

can.title: The Book of Boba Fett
can.reason: Grogu's choice between Jedi training and staying with Din — the emotional hinge of his arc — plays out in this show's later chapters.

must.title: Avengers: Endgame
must.reason: The show opens directly from Wanda's grief over Vision's death and her isolation after the final battle here — the entire premise is her coping with that loss.

can.title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
can.reason: Vision's creation and his and Wanda's first real connection happen in this film, giving weight to what she's recreating in Westview.

must.title: Avengers: Endgame
must.reason: This Loki only exists because the 2012 version escapes with the Tesseract during Endgame's time heist — without that scene there's no explanation for how he's alive or where he is.

must.title: Avengers: Endgame
must.reason: Clint's guilt and his Ronin killing spree, which the show is actively atoning for, follow directly from Natasha's death and the five-year gap depicted here.

must.title: Black Widow
must.reason: Yelena Belova's entire motivation for hunting Clint — believing he murdered her sister Natasha — and her established skills and gear come directly from this film.

must.title: Captain Marvel
must.reason: Nick Fury's decades-long alliance with Talos and the Skrulls' displaced, homeless status — the whole engine of the invasion plot — is established here.

can.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
can.reason: This film's mid-credits reveal that 'Fury' had actually been Talos in disguise for its entire runtime is the exact kind of Skrull-impersonation twist the show's paranoia is built on.

can.title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
can.reason: The season's cold-open illegal cage match against Abomination directly continues that film's post-credits scene, where Wong recruits him to fight.

must.title: Captain Marvel
must.reason: Direct continuation of Carol Danvers' story, powers and unresolved relationships from the first film.

must.title: Ms. Marvel
must.reason: Kamala Khan's bangle and the light-based entanglement power at the center of the plot are established across this show.

must.title: WandaVision
must.reason: Monica Rambeau's light-based powers come specifically from crossing the Hex's energy barrier in this show's finale.

must.title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story

can.reason: Ahsoka's identity as Anakin Skywalker's former padawan, and the relationships that still define her, are built across this series.

must.reason: Wolverine is sent back to 1973 to the exact point where First Class left off, to change history alongside young Xavier and Magneto.

must.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
must.reason: Continues directly from the rewritten timeline and status quo Days of Future Past leaves the team in.

must.title: X-Men: Apocalypse
must.reason: Direct continuation of this cast and timeline, picking up Jean Grey's growing powers seeded there.

must.reason: This Wolverine variant is explicitly running from the fate — and the timeline's end — depicted in Logan; the film's plot hinges on that specific death.

can.reason: The TVA, Mobius, Paradox and the 'Sacred Timeline' pruning mechanics used as plot devices throughout the film are established in this show.

must.reason: Follows the post-Titan-emergence world and Monarch's expanded operations established there.

must.title: Kong: Skull Island
must.reason: Kong's character, Monarch's history with him, and the Hollow Earth concept all come directly from this film.

from.title: Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire
